card.hook: Fifty-six domes and four slim minarets, all in one pale, tidy building. It's a pattern-lover's dream, and the shapes do half the work for you.
card.stand_here: Head to Quba Mosque in Medina. From there it's about 1 minute on foot, heading west, to the mosque. Stop in the open front courtyard and face the domes and minarets.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to show the mosque in its setting. If the whole building won't fit, try zoom 0.5x. Then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the row of domes and the minarets.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line a minaret up with a vertical line so it stands straight, with a little sky above it.
card.best_time: Morning should suit this view, as the sun should be behind you and light up the front of the mosque. Late afternoon is a good second choice for softer light. Fridays are said to be the busiest, so pick a quieter moment if you can.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone has it, and keep the mosque over your shoulder. Hold the phone a bit higher and step back so the domes and minarets fit behind you.
card.ask_someone: In the open front courtyard, ask a passer-by to stand a little back from you and frame you with the domes and minarets behind, then have them check the framing before they tap.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working place of worship, so dress modestly, be discreet around people at prayer and don't point your phone at worshippers. Photos inside the mosque are usually not allowed, so keep your phone away in the prayer areas.
card.challenge: Get a minaret perfectly straight on a gridline with a sliver of sky above it, then see if you can fit a few of those 56 domes in too.
card.good_to_know: Quba Mosque is thought to be the first mosque in the world, first built in the 7th century during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad. The building you see today is a complete reconstruction begun in 1984 and inaugurated on 2 November 1986, designed by Egyptian architect Abdel-Wahed El-Wakil in a traditional style. A larger expansion of the mosque and its surroundings was announced in 2022, so the area around it may look different from visit to visit.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head to Quba Mosque in Medina. From there it's about 1 minute on foot, heading west, to the mosque. Stop in the open front courtyard and face the domes and minarets.

card.hook: The Prophet's Mosque is far too big for one phone photo, and that's the fun part. You get to pick the star of your shot: the long front, one tall minaret, or the green dome.
card.stand_here: For the Prophet's Mosque, stand at the phone icon on the map, about 140 m south of the numbered pin, and face north. You'll be framing one part of the mosque, not all of it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to get the full width of the mosque, then try 1x for a more natural view of one section. For the Green Dome and the tops of the minarets, go to 2x-5x, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the bright stonework, then slide the brightness down a little so the white walls keep their detail.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, when the light is soft and it's quieter, or after sunset when the mosque is lit up. Prayer times are the busiest, so expect more people then.
card.selfie_here: Try the main courtyard, among the giant umbrellas, with the Green Dome behind you. Guides say the courtyard gives the clearest view of the dome against the sky. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x, and hold your phone a bit lower so the dome sits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: In the main courtyard, ask a passer-by to stand back far enough to fit the mosque front and the umbrellas in the frame, while you stand among the umbrellas.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos are generally fine in the outer courtyards and public areas, but not inside the prayer halls or near the Prophet's tomb. Don't film people without their consent, and stop right away if security asks you to. Rules can change, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Line up one minaret with a gridline so it stands perfectly straight, with a little sky above it.
card.good_to_know: The first building dates from 622 and began as an open-air space used as a community centre, a court and a religious school. It's the second mosque the Prophet Muhammad built in Medina, after Quba Mosque. The Green Dome sits at the south-east corner, and in 1909 the mosque became the first place in the Arabian Peninsula with electric lights.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: For the Prophet's Mosque, stand at the phone icon on the map, about 140 m south of the numbered pin, and face north. You'll be framing one part of the mosque, not all of it.

card.hook: Some gates just want their photo taken. The main entrance of the Islamic University of Madinah is big, symmetrical and easy to read, so even a quick snap looks tidy.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 620 m west of the subject, and face east toward the main gate on the city side. The campus lies beyond it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a straight-on view of the whole gateway. Tap zoom 0.5x only if you end up close and the portal won't fit, or try zoom 2x to 5x for a tighter shot of the gate.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the centre of the gateway on the middle line, and keep your phone upright so the sides don't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the gateway than the middle of the day.
card.selfie_here: Try the grand entrance gates on Prince Naif Ibn Abdulaziz Road: use the front camera, tap zoom 0.5x and tilt the phone so the gateway sits over your shoulder. We don't have an exact standing spot for this one, so have a look around when you get there.
card.rules_and_safety: Keep to the public frontage. Administrative areas, classrooms and student residences need university permits. Photography is generally fine in public areas, but be discreet, ask before photographing anywhere sensitive, and don't point your phone at students or staff without asking.
card.challenge: Take three frames of the gate, and see if you can catch one with the road empty and the sides perfectly straight.
card.good_to_know: The Islamic University of Madinah is a public university founded by royal decree in 1961. It started with Islamic studies. Today it also teaches Arabic, law, business, computing, engineering and the sciences.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, about 620 m west of the subject, and face east toward the main gate on the city side. The campus lies beyond it.
